principle: Faster dev cycles via PARALLEL agents that never edit the same file at once. Two guarantees: (1) every lane runs in its OWN git worktree (a separate working directory + branch), so it is physically impossible for two agents to write the same file in the same tree; (2) lanes own DISJOINT file globs, so even at merge time their diffs do not overlap. Results merge back via PR. Heterogeneous brains: cheap Ollama agents (GLM-5.2 / Kimi via the default brain) take the narrow/deterministic/templated lanes; Claude Code agents take the ambiguous/design lanes — the unbounded->bounded brain policy applied to the dev fleet itself.

ollama.use_for: narrow / deterministic / templated lanes; OpenAI-compatible agent pointed at the local Ollama endpoint (GLM-5.2 / Kimi via OLLAMA_API_KEY)

shared_serialized.why: these files are touched by EVERY increment (the proof registry + the computed proof-count token), so they are the #1 source of parallel-edit conflicts. They are owned by NO lane; a lane's proof registration + token bump are applied by the coordinator at MERGE time, one lane at a time (serialized), never concurrently.

lanes.surface: document extraction cascade + the write-in demo

lanes.why_brain: narrow clean-room rule coding over public rules (cheap-brain floor)
templated prose generated from a spec
cross-axis reasoning over the optimization graph
